description: In this project I’m working solo: I’m Viola Zeneli, a Software Engineering graduate from Albania and the only member of Team Viola Fusion. For the “Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots” challenge I built VATRA, Albania’s Fire Calendar, which joins NASA FIRMS fire data from 2000 to 2026 into one record, with a burning activity calendar, fire map, PDF reports, a kids’ game and a built-in guide. I love data, AI, Earth observation and open science.
summary:
VATRA: Albania’s Fire Calendar is a free web app, in English and Albanian, that joins NASA FIRMS active fire data from MODIS (since 2000) and VIIRS (since 2012) into one fire record for Albania, 2000–2026. It shows the record as a burning activity calendar for any area and dates.

It addresses the challenge directly. VIIRS sees many more small hotspots than MODIS, so raw counts jump in 2012 even when fires do not. VATRA counts each ~1 km cell once per day per satellite and calibrates every VIIRS satellite to the MODIS scale by season, so the satellite no longer matters. Tested on years never used for fitting, it reaches Pearson r = 0.99.

It matters because raw counts suggest fires rose 194% after 2012, while the harmonized record shows a 29% drop. As MODIS retires, firefighters, towns and scientists keep one consistent 26-year record to plan before summer. The code, data and report are open on Zenodo.
details:
Try it: https://vatra-albania.streamlit.app
Code: https://github.com/violazeneli31/vatra-albania-fire-calendar
Demo video: https://youtu.be/OU0LoOLec1c

What it does
VATRA joins NASA’s two generations of fire satellites, MODIS (Terra, Aqua; 2000–) and VIIRS (S-NPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21; 2012–), into one record for Albania, 2000–2026. Users pick any area (country, 12 counties, 61 municipalities, or a box or polygon drawn on the map) and any dates. VATRA then shows a burning activity calendar (months × years), how this month compares with normal, trends, the biggest fire events, and the raw vs harmonized difference.

How it works

  1. Load all NASA FIRMS archive and near-real-time files. Remove duplicates, static sources (factories, offshore) and points outside Albania: 109,382 rows become 105,051 clean detections.
  2. Snap each detection to a 0.01° (~1 km) grid and count each cell once per day per satellite (“fire cell-days”). This removes most of the effect of VIIRS splitting one fire into many small pixels.
  3. Calibrate log(MODIS+1) = a + b·log(VIIRS+1) on monthly cell-days, for each VIIRS satellite and season (fire season May–Oct, off-season Nov–Apr). From 2012 the record is the mean of the calibrated VIIRS satellites, so it does not jump when a new satellite joins. Every cell-day gets a weight, so any drawn area is harmonized too.
  4. Validate: fit on 2012–2019, test on 2020–2025 (72 months never used): Pearson r = 0.99, Spearman ρ = 0.96, bias −11%. Against EFFIS burnt areas (yearly): Pearson r = 0.86, Spearman ρ = 0.94.

Main findings
Raw counts suggest fires rose 194% after 2012. The harmonized record shows −29%: the jump came from the new satellite, not new fires. There is no clear trend over 2003–2025 (Mann–Kendall p = 0.43). The fire season peaks in August, the worst year was 2007, and Vlorë has the most fire activity. The record contains 2,774 fire events.

Benefits and impact
Albania has no firefighting planes of its own and depends on help from neighbours every summer. VATRA gives firefighters, municipalities, scientists and schools one consistent, free history of when and where Albania burns, so they can plan before the fire season. As MODIS retires, it keeps the 26-year record usable. Albania is set in one config file, so any country can reuse the method.

Features
English and Albanian, light and dark mode, phone-friendly; calendar with an embroidery view (Albanian cross-stitch poster); fire map with drawing tools; compare years; county stories; PDF reports; CSV downloads; a kids’ game “Sky Twins” with a certificate; and “Viola”, a guide with prepared answers from the data. The latest days come from the FIRMS API.

Creativity
The design comes from Albanian folk embroidery, and the calendar can be shown as a cross-stitch pattern. The name means “the hearth”: fire as something we care for, not something we fear.

Tools
Python, Streamlit, pandas, NumPy, SciPy, pymannkendall, GeoPandas, Shapely, Plotly, Folium, fpdf2, Matplotlib; GitHub; Streamlit Community Cloud; Zenodo.

Open science
Software: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24231571
Dataset: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24231762
Technical report: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24232403
Code under MIT, data under CC BY 4.0.

Limitations
Hotspots show heat at satellite pass time, not burnt area. Harmonized values are estimates with an uncertainty band. There are few NOAA-20/21 overlap months, and MODIS orbit drift affects recent years. VATRA is not an official warning service.

Use of AI (SI)
Claude (Anthropic) helped with code, text, design and the demo video edit. The guide photo of Viola is a real photo with traditional clothing added using ChatGPT, and it is marked “AI-edited photo” in the app, video and thumbnail. The demo voice-over was generated with Kokoro (open-source text-to-speech). The background music was generated in code. All numbers are computed by the code from the data. NASA logos are not used anywhere.
